# 05 Wire core sequence diagrams into render() end to end, add demo

## Outcome

`render(source, container)` recognizes a `sequenceDiagram` document, runs
`buildSequenceModel`→`layoutSequence`→`renderSequenceToSVG`, mounts the resulting SVG, and returns
`controller: null`. A new `demos/sequence-diagram.html`, built against the real `@siren/core` Vite
bundle, visibly renders a core sequence diagram (participants, actors, all ten arrow forms, title,
autonumber) in a browser. This is the first real, demoable milestone for the feature.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `render()` on a real `sequenceDiagram` source string (not a hand-built fixture) mounts an
  SVG into `container` and returns `controller: null`, `diagnostics: []` for valid input.
- [ ] `render()` on a `flowchart` source string is unaffected — same SVG, same controller
  behavior as before this whole board.
- [ ] `render()` on a `sequenceDiagram` source referencing an undeclared participant returns the
  graph-model's error diagnostic and does not throw.
- [ ] `demos/sequence-diagram.html` opened in a browser shows a real sequence diagram exercising
  every core-wave feature (both `participant` and `actor`, all ten arrow forms, `title`,
  `autonumber`).

## Test seam

`render(source: string, container: HTMLElement, options?): SirenRenderResult` — integration test
under jsdom, exercising the full core-wave pipeline end to end.

## Write ownership

- `packages/core/src/index.ts`
- `packages/core/src/index.test.ts` (extend: sequence-diagram cases)

- `examples/*.srn` or inline example source used by the demo (new file, naming at implementer's
